messages:
mia (product): Thinking about a paced rollout for the EU Dedicated cohort — want to combine time-window pacing with cost-aware fallbacks. Goal: avoid sudden quota spikes for customers on reserved capacity while keeping latency SLAs. Thoughts?
raj (eng-sre): +1. key ask: define the pacing window (hours/day) and the trigger to step down to fallback model/region. also: how do we surface SLA crediting if we throttle? :thinking_face:
sam (sales): Customers care about predictability. If we throttle them we need clear SLO impact language and automatic notifications. Prefer soft-throttles first, then degrade model quality as last resort.
jules (eng-platform): We can implement a sliding window token budget per tenant tied to ReservedCapacity usage. Proposal: 3 buckets — green (<=70% budget), amber (70-90%), red (>90%). Amber: notify + reduce burst cap by 30%. Red: route to fallback variant (quantized or smaller model) + email + console flag.
lina (eng-runtime): Implementation notes: runtime already supports model variants and quantization. We need a routing policy that checks tenant_budget_state and prefers same-region fallback before cross-region. Example rule: ``if tenant_state == red && region_capacity_low then route -> local-quantized; else route -> eu-sibling``. Also need KV key TTL for budget windows.
raj (eng-sre): Ops concerns: cross-region fallback increases egress and legal complexity for EU regulated customers. Any cross-region fallback must be opt-in per tenant. Also add a fast rollback (kill-switch) if latency or error rates spike after fallback.
mia (product): Good call re: opt-in for cross-region. For EU regulated customers we should default to local-quantized only and provide an opt-in checkbox for cross-region routing with consent record.
ops-oncall: Suggest adding a circuit-breaker metric: sustained 5m p95 latency increase > 200ms OR error rate > 1% triggers auto-failback to last-known-good variant + page. That gives us quick mitigation.
jules (eng-platform): Agreed. For telemetry we should log: tenant_id, bucket_state, fallback_type, decision_reason, decision_ts. Keep retention 30d for debugging. Also include a sampling stream for postmortem traces.
sam (sales): Can we expose this in console as "Pacing & Fallback" where customer sees current bucket, estimated hourly budget, and option to opt-in to cross-region? That reduces support load.
lina (eng-runtime): Minor engineering constraint: switching a tenant's routing variant is cheap if using policy tokens; pushing per-tenant flags at scale needs batching. We'll need a rollout plan for the flag itself (canary the flag push).
mia (product): Proposed launch criteria: 1) Policy engine + per-tenant buckets implemented; 2) Console UI for opt-in + tenant-visible budget; 3) Telemetry & alerting hooks validated in canary tenants (5 internal tenants); 4) Legal signoff for EU cross-region opt-in. If all green, soft launch to 10% of Dedicated EU customers.
raj (eng-sre): Add a preflight checklist item: simulate 2x traffic spike in staging with mixed fallback routing to ensure no request amplification or KV hot-keys.
ops-oncall: I'll own runbook snippets: how to flip global kill-switch, how to restore per-tenant routing, and SLA credit calc notes.
mia (product): Thanks — next steps: jules/lina pair to draft API + policy spec, raj to add staging test plan, sam to collect top 5 legal-sensitive customers for opt-in language. We can sync tomorrow 10:30. :thumbsup:
